submission.natural_language_explanation: L23/H4 is a fuzzy induction (copy) head: by default it parks almost all of its attention on the window's first token, where its write sits at the floor, so ordinary running prose reads inactive (20 of 20 varied prose sentences peaked at 0.08 of the 25.10 maximum or less, and a window containing standalone digits or rare names but no repeat stayed at 0.08). When the current token X also occurred earlier in the window with a similar preceding token (a space before a numeral, a repeated 'the', a repeated proper noun or identifier), it attends instead to the token Y that followed the earlier copy at weight 0.4-0.95 and copies Y into the residual, giving 0.2-0.7 of max when Y is a digit or short piece continuing a repeated numeral, subword or name ('4712'...'4712' 0.63, '19.83'...'19.83' 0.66, 'Reykjavik'...'Reykjavik' 0.58, '3.14' twice in code 0.49) and 0.15-0.4 when Y is an ordinary word ('spoke' 0.37, 'reviewed' 0.36); in 14 of the scan's 20 top examples the peak's attention (0.35-0.95) lands exactly on that successor, whose predecessor also matched, and the other six are the same copy rule on a repeated range or name ('520-531' -> the '5' three back, 'Lindegaard' -> the 'de' pieces of earlier mentions) or the window's own first token. It stays at the floor when the repeat's preceding token differs ('... we drove to the station, then we drove to the harbour' 0.00), when a distinctive token appears only once, and when the copy target is a sentence-final period or line break.

rival_explanations: It is a numeral-and-range head rather than a general copy head: it fires on written numbers and citation or page ranges because it copies the first digit of a repeated or ranged numeral ('520-531', '716-719', 'D1702 to D1706', '3.14' twice), and the word- and name-repeat peaks in the top examples are incidental, so it should stay inactive on repeated words and code identifiers that contain no digits.

It is a duplicate-token head: it attends to the previous occurrence of the same token (fuzzily, across subword splits and leading spaces), so any token that recurs within the window - even a single common word or a repeated punctuation mark - should drive it, and its alignment to the token after that copy is only a recency artifact.

A six-token code run repeats, so ' print' and ' parse' recur after identical predecessors and copy the code tokens that followed the earlier copies, testing the copy claim on code with no digits at all.

adversarial_test_results.detail: The five-token run ' a Reikiavik' repeats in Spanish, so the name's subword pieces recur after an identical predecessor and copy the earlier successor ' sal', a cross-language holdout of the copy rule.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Every table lists the ratio 3.14 and the appendix restates the ratio 3.14 without rounding.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The run ' the ratio 3.14' repeats, so the decimal's digit tokens recur after identical predecessors and copy a digit, a digit-copy holdout with no page range involved.

adversarial_test_results.detail: The run ' rev42' repeats, so ' 4' recurs after the identical predecessor ' rev' and copies the earlier successor ' 2', testing the hypothesis's fuzzy subword match rather than a whole-word repeat.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A small team spent the winter cataloguing lichens along the coast, photographing each specimen and measuring its growth. They returned to the same cliffs, and the same team resumed measuring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The two-token run ' the same' recurs late in the passage, so at the second ' same' the predecessor ' the' matches and the earlier successor ' cliffs' is copied, a copy well after the opening tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The Lessee shall pay the rent on the first day, and the Lessor may adjust the rent on the first day of any renewal term.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A six-token run ' the rent on the first day' repeats in a legal register unlike the scan corpus, so ' rent' and ' day' recur after identical predecessors and copy their earlier successors.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A warden checked every gate before dawn; after lunch a guard inspected every lock in the same building.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The only repeated token is ' every', preceded by ' checked' once and ' inspected' the other time, so the hypothesis predicts the floor while a duplicate-token head should still fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The astronomer noted that Betelgeuse dimmed sharply during the winter of a quieter decade, and the observatory kept recording its light every clear night.
adversarial_test_results.detail: No content or numeral token recurs and the only repeat is ' the' after different predecessors, the hypothesis's unique-token inactive case, though the recurring ' the' alone should satisfy the duplicate-token rival.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The recipe calls for 3 eggs, a pinch of salt and a little grated nutmeg, stirred into warm milk.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The digit ' 3' appears once and the only repeats are ' a' and ',' after different predecessors, the hypothesis's standalone-digit inactive case.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The eastern gate shut early, and the western gate stayed open.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Repeated noun ' gate' after different predecessors (' eastern' vs ' western') with no other matched repeat, so the hypothesis predicts the floor while a duplicate-token head should attend to the earlier ' gate'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We walked past a bank on the corner and later photographed the bank from across the street, though the light had already faded.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same-word-other-sense probe: ' bank' recurs after ' a' once and ' the' the other time and every ' the' has a different predecessor, so the hypothesis predicts no copy while a duplicate-token head should match.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When the clerk asked about the refund, he said yes. When the manager called hours later, she also said yes.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The run ' said yes.' repeats, so at the second ' yes' the predecessor ' said' matches but the earlier successor is the sentence-final '.', the hypothesis's named exception that keeps the head at the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A whisper in an empty hall is quiet. The forest at noon in winter is quiet too.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The floor was dry. The empty storeroom was dry as well.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She packed apples, pears, plums and figs into a basket before the rain started, and carried it to the van.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The narrow route felt shorter, and the coastal route seemed shorter by noon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Repeated tokens ' route' and ' shorter' each follow a different predecessor (' narrow'/' coastal', ' felt'/' seemed'), so the hypothesis predicts no copy while a duplicate-token head should fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The library keeps its older maps in a cool basement room, and a volunteer repairs torn pages there on most Thursday afternoons, using paste made from wheat starch.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Varied running prose whose only repeats are ' a' and ',' after different predecessors, the hypothesis's claimed default inactive case for ordinary text.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El tren llegó a la estación del norte; más tarde el autobús llegó al sur de la ciudad, con retraso.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish hard negative in the same script as the English examples: ' llegó' and ' la' recur only after different predecessors, the hypothesis's differing-predecessor class in another language.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The gauge read 12 at dawn, 47 at noon and 305 at dusk, then settled.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Standalone distinct numerals with a different lead-in before each, so no digit, space or comma token recurs after an identical predecessor; the hypothesis's named no-repeat digit window should stay at the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Customers trust a brand since the packaging is sturdy, and engineers trust this brand because its battery lasts longer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' trust' and ' brand' recur but each time after a different predecessor, so the hypothesis predicts no copy while duplicate-token attention should still find them.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The citation style guide asks for a page range using an en dash between two numbers, never a hyphen.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Mentions the range topic and an en dash word with no repeated or ranged numeral, testing that topic vocabulary alone does not activate the head.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The crew will run the final test, and the run takes about an hour, so plan the schedule carefully.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Part-of-speech near-miss: ' run' recurs as a verb and as a noun after different predecessors (' will' vs ' the'), which the hypothesis says prevents a match while the duplicate-token rival predicts a hit.
